Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

AMENDMENT NO. 1 JULY 2003 

TO 

IS 8688:1988 SPECIFICATION FOR PLASTIC POTABLE 

WATER BOTTLES 

( First Revision ) 

( Page 1, clause 0.1 ) — Insert the following new clause after 0.1 and 
renumber the subsequent clause 

4 0.2 A scheme of labelling environment friendly products with the ECO logo has 
been introduced at the instance of the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MEF), 
Government of India The ECOMark is being administered by the Bureau of Indian 
Standards (BIS) under the BIS Act, 1986 as per the Resolutions No 71 dated 21 
February 1991 and No 425 dated 28 October 1992 published in the Gazette of the 
Government of India For a product to be eligible for marking with the ECO logo, it 
shall also carry the ISI Mark of the BIS besides meeting additional environment 
friendly requirements For this purpose the Standard Mark would be a single mark 
being a combmauon of the ISI Mark and the ECO logo 

This amendment is based on the gazette NouficaUon No 170 dated 18 May 1996 for 
plastic products as environment friendly products published in the Gazette of the 
Government of India This amendment is, therefore, being issued to this standard to 
include environment friendly requirements for plastic potable water bottles' 

( Page 2, clause 5.1 ) — Insert the following new clause after 5.1 and 
renumber the subsequent clauses 

'6 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR ECO-MARK 

6.1 General Requirements 

6.1.1 The product shall conform to the requirements for quality, safety and 
performance prescribed 

6.1.2 The manufacturer shall produce to BIS the consent clearance as per the 
provisions of Water (Prevention A Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and Air 
(Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act* 1981 along with the authorization, if 
required under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the Rules made thereunder 
while applying for the ECO-Mark The manufacturer shall produce documentary 



Amend No. 1 to IS 8688 : 1988 



evidence with respect to the compliance of regulation under Prevention of Food 
Adulteration Acu 1954 and Drugs and Cosmetic Act, 1940 and Rules made 
thereunder, wherever necessary. 

6.13 The product must display a list of critical ingredients in descending order of 
quantity present expressed as percent of the total. The list of such ingredients shall 
be identified by Bureau of Indian Standards. 

6*1.4 The product packaging shall display in brief the criteria based on which the 
product has been labelled as 'Environment Friendly*. 

6.1.5 The material used for product packaging shall be recyclable or biodegradable. 

6.1.6 It shall also suitably mention that ECO-Mark label is applicable only to the 
packaging material/package, if content is not separately covered under ECO-Mark. 
It may be stated that ECO-Mark is applicable to the product or packaging material or 

both. 

6.2 Product Specific Requirements 

For the manufacture of this product one or more of the virgin material covered in 
following Indian Standards shall be used:

4 REQUIREMENTS 

4.1 Material 

4.1.1 All components oi water bottle (including the bottle 
itself, the cap and the dunking cup) which come in contact 
with water shall be manufactuied from HDPI PVC PP 
and PET conforming to ihe following Indian Standards

4. 1.2 I Ik bottle shall he coloured, pigmented and opaque 

I he colouianls and pigments used shall conform to the

4.1.3 The hanging cord or straps, i( provided, shall be of 
a flexible matciial which is not affected by water 

4.2 Capacity 

4.2.1 I he bottles shall be manulactuied in nominal 
capacity of 500 ml 7S0ml, I 000 nil and 1 SOOmloiany 
other capacity as agreed lo between the puichasei and 
the supplier 

4.2.2 I he biimful capacity shall exceed the nominal 
capacity by a minimum of S percent Hie brunt ul capacity 
shall be deteimined by the method prescubed in IS 279X 

4.3 Design 

I he bottle design shall be such that it is stable when kept 
in \eitical position The shape of the bottle shall be as 
agreed to between the put chaser and the supphei 

4.4 Neck Size 

I he neck shall be of nominal si/e 2S mm, 28 mm, 11 5 
mm or 16 win pilfer proof finish | see IS 7*S J 1 (Part 4)| 

4.5 Cap 

I he bottle shall be closed with a suitable closure made of 
mclaloi [>lastics and pilfei proof in character Additional 
protection shall be made by using printed shrink sleeves 
or similar measures 

4.6 Cup 

1 he bottle may be piovided with a drinking cup, which 
shall tit on to the bottle neck 

4.7 Hanging Cord or Strap 

A flexible hanging cord or strap to hang the bottle on 
shoulder tn peg may be piovided with the bottle It may 
be hinged or snapped to the body ol the bottle 

4.8 Workmanship and Finish 

1 he bottle shall be tnanulaclured in accordance with good 
manufacturing practices These shall be tree from 
manufaetuiing defects such as foreign particles, burnt, 
oxidized or unhomogem/ed mattei, flash, rocking bottom,

4.9 Odour 

I he bottles shall be bee from any odour, dirt or dust 
pai tides 



4.10 Mass 

The mass of the bodies shall be as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier There shall be a tolerance of 
± 5 percent on the agreed mass

on agreed dimensions shall be as follows 

a) Up to and including 100 mm ± 1 5 mm 

b) Over 100 mm and up to 200 mm ±20 mm 

c) Over 200 mm ± 2 S mm 

4.12 Overall Migration 

The limit of overall migration with water when tested as 
prescribed m IS 9X4 S shall not exceed 60mg/l of simulant 
and 10 rng/dnrof the surface ol the container 

4.13 Tests 

4.13.1 Closure Leaka^i Test 

The bottle shall he tilled to Us nominal capacity with 
coloured walci at ambient tempeiature and closed tightly 
with tire cap I he stopper plug, where provided shall be 
pressed tight in position and the cap shall be fitted tight 
by hand The filled bottle shall be kept in \eitically 
inverted position over a piece of blotting paper foi a period 
of \() mm At the end of the test, the closure shall not 
show an) leakage of watei 

4.13.2 Drop lrnptu t 7t W 

The bottle with the cap but without the dunking cup, when 
sub|ected to the drop test as piescnbed in IS 2798 shall 
not show any sign of cracking Slight deshaping of the 
body shall not rendei the bottles unacceptable in the test 

4.13.3 Hanging Cord/Strap Strength Test 

I he hanging eord/stiap shall be able to support the mass 
equal to 1 times the mass of filled bottle tor 10 mm without 
breaking The elongation under load shall not exceed 10 
percent of the total length of the cord Initial stretching 
due to unwinding of the coid shall not be taken as 
elongation tot the purpose ot calculation 

5 WATER POTABILITY TEST 

Potable water stored in the bottle lor 72 h shall not acquire 
any unpleasant odour or bitter taste or shall not impair 
the health when tested according to the method prescribed 
in Annex A 



IS 8688 : 2004

ANNEX A 
(Clause 5) 

METHOD OF TEST FOR POTABILITY OF WATER 
STORED IN PLASTICS BOTTLES 



A-I GENERAL 

A-Ll Odour of water, though very important, cannot 
be determined in absolute units Olfactory sense, which 
is most sensitive means of detecting small concentration 
of odiferous substances, lacks piecision and 
mathematical expression neveitheless a quantitative test 
is presciibcd 

A-I.2 The watei for testing shall be clear and fresh free 
(mm any suspended oi dissolved impurities It 
necessary it may be hltued before storage 



A-2 PROCEDURE 

Heal the water to a temperature of ^8 ± 2"C and fill the 
bottles to its nominal capacity and close tightly with the 
cap Keep the bottles at 18 ± 2 C for a period of 72 h at 
ambient temperature 

A-3 OBSERVATIONS 

At the end of 72 h the water shall not give any unpleasant 
odour oi taste Any visible fungus giowth in water shall 
rendci the bottle matcnal unfit loi use
